alerts.title: TDF renal toxicity: eGFR 52, rising creatinine
alerts.message: Guidelines state that if GFR is <60 mL/min, TDF should be substituted with ABC. Patient's creatinine has steadily risen from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL with eGFR now 52 mL/min, meeting the TDF contraindication threshold. TDF is a known cause of chronic kidney disease, Fanconi syndrome, and acute kidney injury. Evidence for drug attribution includes the progressive decline temporally linked to 3 years of TDF exposure and urinalysis showing proteinuria. Evidence against includes the absence of Fanconi-specific findings (no glycosuria beyond trace, no hypophosphatemia documented) and no alternative cause identified. Occasional ibuprofen use may also contribute to renal injury. The guideline action is to substitute TDF with ABC if GFR <60.

evidence.recommended_action: Substitute TDF with ABC (ABC/3TC/DTG) given eGFR 52 <60 threshold. Conduct renal ultrasound and consider nephrology referral for progressive CKD.

alerts.title: TDF plus regular ibuprofen: compounded nephrotoxicity risk
alerts.message: Patient takes ibuprofen 400mg 2-3 times weekly for 6 months while on TDF. TDF is nephrotoxic and guidelines list CKD and acute kidney injury as major TDF toxicities. NSAIDs including ibuprofen reduce renal perfusion via prostaglandin inhibition and can precipitate acute kidney injury, especially combined with TDF. The compounding risk of TDF nephrotoxicity plus regular NSAID use in a patient with already declining renal function (eGFR 52) significantly increases the probability of further renal deterioration. The patient's rising creatinine trend and proteinuria are consistent with this combined insult.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to discontinue ibuprofen or limit to rare, single doses. Consider alternative analgesia such as paracetamol for headaches.

alerts.title: No clinician plan despite renal decline and TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines require health workers to screen for suspected ADRs at each encounter and conduct relevant laboratory investigations when adverse events are suspected. Patient has a clear pattern of progressive renal decline (creatinine 0.9 to 1.4 over 4 years, eGFR 52, proteinuria) on TDF, yet no clinician assessment or plan was documented today. Required actions missing from the plan include: renal function panel with electrolytes, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, renal ultrasound to exclude alternative causes, and a documented decision regarding TDF substitution per guideline thresholds.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment of renal decline, order renal ultrasound and electrolyte panel, complete aDSM form, and plan TDF substitution per guidelines.
